summary.short: Mexico's consolidated Federal Labor Law (text as of 14-05-2026) sets general rules for employment relationships, working hours, wages, rest, profit sharing, dismissal and special worker categories, applying throughout the Republic. Provisions added by DOF 24-12-2024 cover digital platform workers, including limits on reinstatement and severance (Arts. 49, 50, 127).
summary.long: The Ley Federal del Trabajo, in its consolidated text as of 14-05-2026, applies throughout the Republic to employment relations under Article 123(A) of the Constitution. It defines workers, employers and employment relationships, regulates probation, training and fixed-term contracts, and prohibits subcontracting of personnel except for registered specialised services. It sets maximum working hours, overtime limits, rest days, paid vacations, minimum and other wages, wage protections, and worker profit sharing. It governs suspension and termination of employment, reinstatement and compensation, and imposes employer duties on workplace safety, electronic recording of working hours (Art. 132 XXXIV), protocols against discrimination and harassment, and training. Special chapters cover women (maternity protections), minors (minimum age 15, prohibited hazardous work), trust workers, ship and aircraft crews, and other categories. Penalties for certain procedural misconduct are fixed at 100 to 1000 times the Unidad de Medida y Actualización (Art. 48). Provisions added by DOF 24-12-2024 cover digital platform workers: no mandatory reinstatement except for collective-rights violations (Art. 49 VI), a three-month severance plus twenty days' salary per year of service (Art. 50 IV), and profit sharing above 288 hours worked per year (Art. 127 IX). The platform chapter itself (Arts. 291-A et seq.) is outside the fetched part.

notes: Part 1 of 7 covers Arts. 1-220 of the consolidated Ley Federal del Trabajo (texto vigente, última reforma DOF 14-05-2026), not the 24-12-2024 decree as such. Digital-platform provisions in this part appear only as amendment markers: Art. 49 (frs. IV-VI, VI added), Art. 50 (frs. II-IV, IV added) and Art. 127 (frs. VI, VIII, IX; IX added). The platform-worker chapter itself is in later parts. Not coded here although present: the 288-hour profit-sharing threshold (Art. 127 IX) and the three-months-plus-20-days severance formula (Art. 50 IV). Art. 50 IV and Art. 127 IX refer to Art. 291-D, outside this part. Art. 11 names directors as employer representatives. Empty strings stand for null where the schema has no null option (target_instrument_id, lei, ticker). Relation targets are not in the registry as far as this part shows. section_status: relations and entities are populated; status is set to not_applicable only because the schema requires a value. Part 2 of 7 covers Arts. 221 to 413 of the Ley Federal del Trabajo, including Chapter IX BIS on platform work (Arts. 291-A to 291-U, added DOF 24-12-2024). The page headers show the text consolidated to DOF 14-05-2026, while registry metadata lists 2024. Art. 305 Bis (added DOF 14-05-2026) requires contracts for performing artists to specify the conditions and pay for use of their image or voice through artificial intelligence systems or other technology; it is noted here without an obligation row, as only this part is annotated. Art. 291-C treats platform workers below the monthly net income threshold as independent workers but extends listed rights during time worked, except frac. V of 291-C and frac. VI of 291-K. Art. 291-M frac. IV requires three days notice; Art. 291-Q requires notice of not less than fifteen days. Platform operators are the addressees of Chapter IX BIS but are not named in this part, so they are not coded as entities. Relations target instruments outside the registry, so target_instrument_id is left blank. Part 3 of 7 covers LFT arts. 414 to 512-G and the occupational disease table (Art. 513). It contains no provisions on digital platforms and is not AI-specific; it is annotated only for the fields requested. Many articles read Se deroga (e.g., Arts. 421 I-II, 452-468, 470-471). The Tabla de Enfermedades de Trabajo uses WHO CIE-11 codes, which are classification references, not legal instruments. Art. 512-C refers to a future reglamento on safety and health, not identified by name. section_status relations and entities are marked not_applicable only because the entries above are the complete set for this part. Part 4 of 7 covers the end of the history note before Art. 514, Arts. 514 to 526 (review of the disability tables; prescription, Title Ten; labour authorities, Title Eleven), and the disability valuation tables (Tablas I to XV, Tabla de enfermedades de trabajo sections, and the Fletcher formula). Only relations, entities and notes were requested for this part. The disability percentages in the tables are not coded here. Internal references to articles of this Law (e.g., Arts. 17, 492, 494, 521, 684-B) are not coded as relations. The text marks Art. 523 fractions IX and XII and Art. 525 as repealed (“Se deroga”). The Catálogo de las Cédulas is referred to but is not in this part. The text extraction of the tables is garbled in places (e.g., Tablas I–II, VI, VIII–IX, XIII), so table values are not verified against the official PDF. The Art. 514 review obligation has no fixed date beyond “al menos cada cinco años”. Part 5 of 7 (arts. 527-747): federal and local jurisdiction, labour authorities, Servicio Nacional de Empleo, labour inspection, minimum wage and profit-sharing commissions, conciliation (Título Trece Bis) and litigation procedure. No provisions specific to digital platform work appear in this part. Many articles are marked as repealed (e.g., art. 530 Bis, 591-603, 605 Bis-647); repeal dates are as stated in the text. Art. 641-A is noted in the text as not repealed by the DOF 01-05-2019 decree. Sanction and UMA amounts (e.g., arts. 684-E IV, 709-I, 729, 731) are not coded in this part. Relations and entities are the only sections with content here; no obligations, thresholds or definitions were coded. This part (Arts. 774 to 991 Bis) covers evidence, ordinary and special procedures, collective economic conflicts, strikes, execution and remedies. Many articles are marked as repealed by DOF 01-05-2019 or 30-11-2012 (for example Arts. 845-856, 864-869, 875-891, 898-899, 908, 915, 917-918). Those repeal notes are session-law history and were not coded as events. No history note in this part cites DOF 24-12-2024, and no operative provision here concerns digital platform workers. The text is an official consolidated version dated 14-05-2026, which is cited as the reform date at the top of each page. Art. 899-E contains a historical note that paragraphs three to five were derogated by the 2019 reform. Part 7 covers Arts. 992-1010 (penalties), the original 1969 transitional provisions and the transitional articles of amending decrees from 1998 to 2026, as printed in the consolidated text (Última Reforma DOF 14-05-2026). Fines are stated in Unidades de Medida y Actualización (UMA) and are not converted. Amendment history lists decrees that also amend other laws (e.g. the 1 May 2026 decree on the Ley Orgánica de la Administración Pública Federal and the Ley de Comercio Exterior; the 14 May 2026 decree on the Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor); these are not coded here as relations. Possible inconsistency: Art. 1004-B penalises breach of obligations in Art. 15-B, but the 2021 subcontracting decree derogates Arts. 15-A to 15-D, while the penalty text still shows only the 2019 reform date.
